title: Sleepy allocator-induced reserved-pool starvation and customer escalation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Multiple customers experienced sustained request rejects and silent request queuing during short bursts. Root trigger: allocator goroutines entering extended sleep windows under certain lease-reconcile timing, delaying burst credit reclamation and causing reserved pools to appear full to the admission controller. This ticket tracks the emergency mitigation, customer comms, and a robust fix. Impact surface: hosted and dedicated tenants on reserved pools with mixed small/large-tenant cardinality; symptom onset during region-wide traffic spike at ~2026-03-09T21:00Z. Customers affected: Greenline Finance (support escalation), two mid-market customers in EU region. Observed behavior: token-level latency remained normal for admitted requests, but admission rate dropped and requests were soft-queued or rejected with 429-like errors at the API layer. Autoscaler telemetry showed no scale-up due to perceived headroom exhaustion while allocator logs showed long sleep backoff cycles.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy mixed-tenant workload (10 small tenants + 1 large tenant) to a reserved pool with burst enabled
2) Emit rapid microbursts from large tenant (spikes of 300 qps for 30s every 2m) while small tenants generate low baseline traffic
3) Observe allocator logs: lease-reconciler backoff > 60s and allocator goroutines in 'sleepy' state
4) Monitor admission controller: available_slots metrics freeze while queued_requests increases and burst_credit_balance does not decrement as expected
root_cause: A combination of a conservative backoff algorithm in the allocator plus a missed fast-path reclamation when burst credits are available. Under moderate GC/CPU pressure the allocator's jittered sleep extended beyond the burst replenish window; the admission controller depends on a timely lease reconciliation to open slots. Additionally, a race in the burst ledger's reconciliation allowed headroom to be marked as in-use while the actual slot release was not propagated to the admission layer for up to 75s.
mitigations: Immediate (customer-facing): Force-reclaim burst credits for affected pools and temporarily bump burst window for Greenline Finance via admin API (done 2026-03-10T02:15Z)
Hotpatch (within 24h): Short-circuit allocator backoff when pending queued_requests > threshold and wake reconcile on burst-credit-change event (PR linked below)
Short-term (2 weeks): Improve telemetry visibility for allocator sleep time and add alert when headroom propagation latency > 10s
Long-term (Q2): Replace jittered-sleep with event-driven wakeups and simplify burst ledger state transitions to be idempotent and observable
rollout_plan: 1) Canary patch to EU region reserved pools (single AZ) with 10% traffic routing; monitor admission_rate, queued_requests, allocator_sleep_ms for 1 hour
2) If canary stable, expand to other EU pools and then NA pools in 4-hour windows
3) Post-rollout: run synthetic microburst test against all pools on next maintenance window
4) If rollback needed: revert canary changes and reapply forced reclaim script to impacted pools
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: queued_requests > 200 and admission_rate drops by > 30% for > 3m -> Pager and on-call ENG
Synthetic: microburst admission acceptance rate test every 30m
